payload.recallText: A freshman journalism student at Fordham, writes for the Ram newspaper. He comes across a story about Dean McGowan, who wants to enact a policy to make Fordham more prestigious and less friendly to poorer applicants. McGowan is antagonistic when he encounters the student, but a person with a cream pie hits him. The student goes back to the office, his editor Jim Dwyer, a future pulitzer prize winner, tells him to write it up. The student does but he embellishes the encounter, calling the person pie man in a series of stories, gives him a cape. It becomes a recurring story. Pie Man also hits Sheila, the student body president who may be having an affair with Dean McGowan. McGowan also had a policy No Beers at Barbecues. Later on, the student is at a bar. Angela, a girl from his brit lit class, whom he has been flirting with for two months, taps him on the shoulder and asks if he is Pie Man. He knows if he lies, she will have sex with him. He lies. She tells me to buy her a beer and tell her about it.
